title: Fewshot Architectonic — scratch experiments & failure sketches
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for a new angle on few-shot construction: think of exemplar sets as composable architectural pieces (hence "architectonic"). Goal is to move past flat lists of examples and treat slots as roles + constraints + attestations.

Motivation / goal:
- Reduce brittle reordering effects and hunting for the single best exemplar set.
- Make prompt sets easier to mutate programmatically (surgery/replace/expand) with predictable behavior.
- Surface systematic failure modes when we vary one role at a time.

Core hypotheses (to test):
1) Role-stable exemplars: If each exemplar is annotated with a role (instruction, edge-case, clarifier, negative-example), model behavior becomes more predictable when swapping content.
2) Compact attestations: small post-exemplar tokens like "intent: clarify" or "constraint: strict" will reduce hallucination in domain-constraint tasks.
3) Position invariants: some roles prefer early slots, others prefer late; swap tests will reveal these invariants.

Quick experiment matrix (local testing):
- Task: API change summarization (input: diff-like text), target: one-line summary + high-level impact bullets.
- Baseline set: 4 exemplars (mixed). Variant A: re-label roles explicitly at top of each exemplar. Variant B: insert "attestations" after exemplars. Variant C: reorder by role.
- Metrics: accuracy by rubric (0/1 for coverage of required clauses), hallucination rate (mentions non-existent endpoints), leniency of verbosity.

Failure cases observed (notes):
- Model copies exemplar style too literally when exemplar has weird punctuation -> overfitting to stylistic noise. Solution attempt: normalize punctuation in source exemplars and add style-attestation like "tone: concise".
- When negative-exemplar (showing what NOT to do) is placed last, model flips and uses negative behavior as positive instruction. Hypothesis: last-slot salience for negation is high; try double-negation or explicit label.
- Attestations with uncommon tokens (like "constraint: 𝛂-strict") get ignored. Use ASCII tokens only and test tokenization effect.

Examples (raw):
-- exemplar-role: instruction
Input: Replace deprecated /v1/transactions with /v2/transactions in client POST flow; keep schema but add idempotency token.
Output: Summary: Update POST client endpoint to /v2/transactions. Impact: migration required for integrations, add idempotency header X-Idempotency.

-- exemplar-role: negative-example
Input: Add new GET endpoint that returns non-deterministic data.
Output: BAD: Use extensive free-text logs in response.
(Observe: model sometimes echoes BAD pattern as acceptable when negative-example is unlabeled.)

Surgical mutations I want to try programmatically:
- role-swap: keep exemplar content but change role label, run N trials to compute role-sensitivity score per exemplar.
- attestation-ablation: remove attestations and compare hallucination delta.
- density-scan: progressively compress exemplar text to measure minimum info.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to encode multi-turn exemplars (conversations) into architectonic roles? Maybe break into "turn-role" meta-tags.
- Can we build a small DSL for attestations (tone, constraints, evidence-required, fallback-policy) that stays readable?
- Validate on 3 tasks: API summarization, policy extraction (from policy text -> short checklist), and unit-test generation (input: function docstring -> tests).

Experimental notes (short logs):
2025-01-20: ran baseline vs attestation-A on local model q4_1; attestation-A reduced hallucination from 18% -> 10% on small sample (n=50). But variance high.
2025-01-27: role-swap test showed some exemplars are "role-anchored" (model changes output drastically when role label changes) while others are content-anchored (little effect). Need to surface features that predict anchoring (length, specificity, presence of numbers).

Quick heuristics for curating architectonic exemplars:
- Keep one short instruction exemplar (<=40 tokens) as canonical pattern.
- Include one edge-case exemplar that is labelled explicitly as "edge-case" and uses real-ish but synthetic data.
- For negative examples, always prefix with explicit token "NEGATIVE_EX" and close with "END_NEGATIVE" to reduce accidental adoption.
- Standardize attestations with ASCII keys: tone, constraint, role, evidence. Example: "[role:edge-case][tone:precise][constraint:strict]" after exemplar.

Notes to self: avoid elaborate names that confuse the model ("architectonic" is my internal label; keep prompts plain when used in production).

Small TODO list:
- [ ] write a small generator that produces role-swap variants and runs batch experiments (JIRA AI-1428).
- [ ] build rubric for 3 tasks, collect 300 human labels.
- [ ] try attestations with explicit token separators vs inline natural language to measure signal strength.

Links / references: see linked artifacts above. Also cross-check with "fewshot-stability" confluence draft (internal) and earlier "negative-exemplar-balancing-playlog" notes for negative-ex strategies.

End of scratchpad. Will convert high-signal bits into a short playbook once experiments stabilize.
